summary:
Every palindromic substring has a centre: a letter (odd length) or the gap between two letters (even length).
From each of the 2n − 1 centres, expand outward while the two ends match; every successful step is one more
palindrome. O(n²) time, O(1) space.

question.md:
Count palindromic substrings of `s`; equal substrings at different positions count separately.

- **Single letters count.**
- **n ≤ 2000**: about 2 × 10⁶ substrings.

think.md:
`"abaab"` has **8** palindromic substrings: ['a', 'aba', 'b', 'baab', 'a', 'aa', 'a', 'b'].

Checking each substring separately repeats work: if `s[i..j]` is a palindrome, then `s[i−1..j+1]` is one exactly
when its two new ends match. So grow palindromes outward from their centres, and stop at the first mismatch.

idea.md: For every pair `i ≤ j`, test `s[i..j]` with two pointers.

lines.text: Two pointers from its ends; it's a palindrome if they meet without a mismatch.

complexity.md: **Time O(n³)** in the worst case (e.g. all one letter). **Space O(1).**

limits.md: Re-tests the inside of every substring. A palindrome's inside is a smaller palindrome, which a table or centre expansion reuses.

approaches.title: Dynamic programming table

idea.md: `pal[i][j]` is true when `s[i] == s[j]` and (`j − i < 2` or `pal[i+1][j−1]`). Fill by increasing length (or `i` from the end) and count the true cells.

build: Fill from short to long substrings.

lines.text: Rows from the bottom up, so `pal[i+1][…]` is ready when row `i` needs it.
Matching ends around a palindromic (or empty / single) inside.

steps.text: Length 1: every letter. Length 2: equal neighbours.
Longer lengths reuse shorter results; counting the true cells gives 8.

walk.title: dp[i][j] says whether s[i..j] is a palindrome: true when the ends match and the inside is a palindrome.

limits.md: The table is only read one diagonal step away. Expanding from each centre gets the same answers with O(1) memory.

idea.md: For each centre `c` in `0..2n−2` (`i = c / 2`, `j = i + c % 2`): while `s[i] == s[j]`, count one and widen.

lines.text: Even `c`: centre on letter `c/2` (odd-length palindromes). Odd `c`: centre on the gap after it (even lengths).
Each matching step outward is one more palindrome; the first mismatch ends this centre.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** in the worst case (all one letter), much less typically. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: Centre at letter 0: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'a'.
Centre at letter 1: expands 2 step(s); the widest is 'aba'.
Centre at letter 2: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'a'.
Centre at gap 2.5: expands 2 step(s); the widest is 'baab'.
Centre at letter 3: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'a'.
Centre at letter 4: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'b'.

walk.title: Every palindrome has a centre (a letter or a gap). Expand around each of the 2n − 1 centres, counting each successful step.

takeaways.md:
- **Palindromic substrings ↔ centres:** 2n − 1 of them (letters and gaps).
- Expansion is O(n²) with O(1) memory; the DP table is the same idea with O(n²) memory.
- Manacher's algorithm counts them in O(n) (see Palindrome Census).
